asks.notes: "Answer (a) and (b)." prints two separately answered melodies; the scheme marks "Each Melody" on one 20-mark band table, "20 + 20". One ask and one card per melody. Each band joins its three printed marks (20 / 19 / 18 = 18-20 ... 2 / 1 / 0 = 0-2); its first bullet (rhythm and style of dance) is the band label, the other bullets and the two italic lines its guidance. The 2023 Ordinary scheme prints no rhythm notes for Section A, so no task requirements. (b) is the waltz (3/4, F major, Moderato, p).

asks.questionText: Composing melody and bass notes from a set of chords at cadence points Preparatory work: • Write out the scale of D major on the stave below. • Plot the chords available in this key (I, ii, IV, V and vi) either in the chord bank grid or on the stave below. The first chord is given. • Study the piece of music on the following page. • Using the given rhythms, add melody and bass notes to complete the cadences and approach chords as follows: • (i) At A, an imperfect cadence with approach chord (I—IV—V) • (ii) At B, a plagal cadence with approach chord (vi—IV—I) • (iii) At C, an interrupted cadence with approach chord (I—V—vi) • (iv) At D, a perfect cadence with approach chord (ii—V—I)

grid.stem: Answer one question only in this section:
taskRequirements: 1. Same chord in adjacent boxes not accepted
2. Accidental and suffix, where relevant, must be fully correct for mark to be awarded
3. Chords must be part of a good progression
1. No doubling of major 3rd under chord symbol
3. Stepwise movement to and from inversions = good

criteria.label: 1 mark per correct note of chord
1 mark per correct melody note which is part of the given chord and which falls on the correct beat of the bar. The given rhythms must be used. (1 x 12)
Up to 3 marks for quality of correct melody line at each cadence point, which fits well with the chord progression and correct bass notes (3 x 4)
1 mark per correct bass note of the given chord and which falls on the correct beat of the bar. The given rhythms must be used (1 x 12)
Up to 3 marks for quality of the correct bass line at each cadence point (3 x 4)

asks.notes: Section B: the "Preparatory work" (scale and chord bank) is MARKED at Ordinary Level ("Grid / Stave", 1 mark per correct note of chord, 1 x 12), so its bullets are part of the question text and its line is a counted criterion. The chord bank prints I ("The first chord is given") and also iii and vii° already filled in and shaded, outside the five chords asked for (I, ii, IV, V and vi): the 12 notes are those of ii, IV, V and vi; the pre-filled chords are part of the printed question, not separate asks. The four cadence criteria are the scheme's "Criteria for awarding marks at cadence points" lines, each 12 over the four cadences (the per-cadence table A-D prints the same lines at 1 x 3 and 3). The two "Up to 3 marks for quality ... (3 x 4)" lines carry no bands and sit on 0-12. The Section B general points (scheme p6) are carried on all three questions. The 2023 Ordinary scheme prints NO table of given or accepted chords for Q4-Q6, so there is no scheme crop. Q4's (i)-(iv) name the cadences at A-D; one ask, one total.
